{{nihongo|'''Ozu Shrine'''|小津神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Ōmi Province]].

=== Precinct ===
It stands in a forest 4.3 km northwest of {{ill|Moriyama Station (Shiga)|arz|محطة مورياما|eo|Stacio Moriyama (Ŝiga)|fr|Gare de Moriyama (Shiga)|id|Stasiun Moriyama (Shiga)|it|Stazione di Moriyama (Shiga)|ja|守山駅 (滋賀県)|jv|Setatsiyun Moriyama (Shiga)|ko|모리야마역 (시가현)|nl|Station Moriyama|ur|موری یاما اسٹیشن (شیگا)|zh|守山車站 (滋賀縣)|qid=Q1042787|lt=Moriyama Station}}<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.biwako-visitors.jp/spot/detail/168|title=Ozu Shrine | Shiga tourism information|accessdate=2020-04-15|publisher=Biwako Visitors Bureau}}</ref>. The shrine lies at the center of Sugie, a settlement that was a key point for transport on Lake Biwa waterways{{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=184}}. === History ===
The shrine originally worshiped the ancient local Ozu clan; later {{ill|Ukanomitama|de|Ukanomitama|eo|Ukanomitama|fr|Uka-no-Mitama|ja|ウカノミタマ|mni|ꯎꯀꯅꯣꯃꯤꯇꯃ|ru|Ука-но митама|simple|Ukanomitama|sv|Ukanomitama|th|อูกาโนมิตามะ|zh|宇迦之御魂神|qid=Q3080728|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto}} became the principal deity<ref name=":0" />. Shrine records say that in {{ill|567|ab|567|af|567|am|567 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|567|ar|567|ary|567|ast|567|az|567|azb|۵۶۷ (میلادی)|bar|567|be|567|be_x_old|567|bg|567|bn|৫৬৭|bpy|মারি Biwa|ru|Бива (озеро)|simple|Lake Biwa|sl|Biva|sr|Бива (језеро)|sv|Biwasjön|sw|Ziwa Biwa|th|ทะเลสาบบิวะ|tr|Biwa Gölü|uk|Біва (озеро)|uz|Biva|vi|Hồ Biwa|zh|琵琶湖|zh_min_nan|Pî-pê-ô͘|zh_yue|琵琶湖|qid=Q200239}} by flood<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://www.shiga-jinjacho.jp/ycBBS/Board.cgi/02_jinja_db/db/ycDB_02jinja-pc-detail.html?mode:view=1&view:oid=450|title=Shrine introduction: Ozu Shrine (OZU)|accessdate=2020-04-15|publisher=Shiga Prefecture Shrine Office}}</ref>. The dance dedicated by parishioners when welcoming back the divine spirit that had flowed into the lake is said to have become the later Naginata festival<ref>{{Cite book|和書|title=Moriyama City Bulletin|date=2000-05-01|year=2000|publisher=Moriyama City|url=http://www2.city.moriyama.lg.jp/koho/000501/index3.html|accessdate=2020-04-15|page=3}}</ref>. In {{ill|Bun'ō|Q1199883|qid=Q1199883}} 1 ({{ill|1260|Q5508|qid=Q5508}}), offerings from Sagami-no-kami and Echigo-no-kami and donations of Azumigawa fishing grounds were made<ref name=":1" />. Revered by the imperial court and warrior houses, in {{ill|1335|Q6011|qid=Q6011}} ({{ill|Kenmu|Q1193970|qid=Q1193970|lt=Kenmu}} 2) Ashikaga Takauji prohibited armed troops from entering the sacred precinct<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":0" />. The honden burned in the {{ill|Ōnin War|Q385676|qid=Q385676}}, then was rebuilt by {{ill|Rokkaku Takayori|Q2890348|qid=Q2890348}}<ref name=":1" />. It burned again in {{ill|1505|Q6153|qid=Q6153}} ({{ill|Eishō (Muromachi period)|cs|Eišó|fa|ایشو (دوره موروماچی)|fr|Ère Eishō (Muromachi)|ja|永正|ko|에이쇼 (센고쿠 시대)|no|Eishō (Sengoku)|ru|Эйсё|simple|Eishō (Muromachi period)|sr|Еишо (Муромачи период)|sv|Eishō (Sengoku)|tr|Eishō (Muromachi)|zh|永正|qid=Q1193577}} 2) during the Eishō disturbances, but the current honden was rebuilt over 18 years by the Enryakuji monk Myōshunbō Jikkan<ref name=":1" />.

In the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it had 13 nearby villages as ujiko{{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=184}}.

=== Enshrined deities ===
Its principal deity is Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto; later {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|abstract|Q272993|ar|سوسانو|azb|سوسانو|bcl|Susanoo|be|Сусанаа|bg|Сусаноо|ca|Susanoo|cs|Susanoo|da|Susa-no-o|de|Susanoo|el|Σουσάνoο|eo|Susanoo|es|Susanoo|eu|Susanoo|fa|سوسانو (خدا)|fi|Susanoo|fr|Susanoo|hr|Susano|hu|Szuszanoo|hy|Սուսանո|id|Susanoo|it|Susanoo|ja|スサノオ|ka|სუსანოო-ნო-მიკოტო|ko|스사노오|la|Susano'o|lb|Susanoo|mni|ꯁꯨꯁꯅꯨ-ꯅꯣ-ꯃꯤꯀꯣꯇꯣ|nl|Susanoo|pl|Susanoo|pt|Susanoo|ro|Susanoo|rsk|Сусано|ru|Сусаноо|simple|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|sl|Susanovo|sr|Сусаноо|su|Susanoo|sv|Susanoo|ta|சுசானவோ|th|ซูซาโนโอะ|tok|jan sewi Susano|tr|Susanoo|uk|Сусаноо|vi|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|zh|素戔嗚尊|zh_min_nan|Susanoo|qid=Q272993|lt=Susanoo-no-Mikoto}} and {{ill|Kamuo Ichihime|Q11588867|qid=Q11588867|lt=Ōichi-hime-no-Mikoto}} were enshrined as associated deities<ref name=":1" />.

=== Festival ===
Naginata dance is performed every {{ill|May 5|Q2550|qid=Q2550}}<ref name=":0" /> and is designated a national {{ill|National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property|Q6573893|qid=Q6573893}}<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.biwako-visitors.jp/event/detail/118|title=Naginata-furi (Ozu Shrine) | Shiga tourism information|accessdate=2020-04-15|publisher=Biwako Visitors Bureau}}</ref>. With mikoshi procession, ritual performances are dedicated by rotating duty groups of carriers and dancers{{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=184}}. In years when Sugie, Akanoi, Yajima, Miyake, Yamaga, and Ishida serve as dance groups, offerings include naginata-furi and Sanyare dance{{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=184}}. Naginata-furi leads the parade while swinging naginata; Sanyare dancers follow in flower-hat costume with {{ill|Drum|af|Trom|als|Trommel|an|Tambor|ang|Trum|ar|طبل|arz|طبله|ast|Tambor|atj|Tewehikan|az|Baraban|azb|طبیل|ba|Барабан|bar|Drumme|bat_smg|Būgnos|be|Барабан|be_x_old|Барабан|bg|Барабан|bn|ড্রাম|bo|རྔ།|br|Taboulin|bs|Bubanj|bxr|Хэнгэрэг|ca|Tambor|chy|Onéhavo'e|ckb|تەپڵ|crh|Davul|cs|Buben|cv|Параппан|cy|Drwm|da|Tromme|de|Trommel|el|Τύμπανο|eo|Tamburo|es|Tambor|et|Trumm|eu|Danbor|fa|طبل|fi|Rumpu|fj|Lali|fr|Tambour (instrument)|fy|Tromme|ga|Druma|gl|Tambor|gn|Angu'a (tembipu)|guc|Kaasha|ha|Ganga|hak|Kú|he|תוף|hi|ड्रम|hif|Dhol|hr|Bubanj|ht|Drum|hu|Dob (hangszer)|hy|Թմբուկ|id|Drum|ilo|Tambor|io|Tamburo|is|Tromma|it|Tamburo|iu|ᕿᓚᐅᑦ|ja|太鼓|jv|Drum|kk|Барабан|km|ស្គរ|ko|북|kv|Барабан|kw|Tabour|ky|Барабан|la|Tympanum|lez|Далдам|li|Tróm|lmo|Tambur|ln|Mbonda|lt|Būgnas|lv|Bungas|mad|Drum|mg|Amponga|mk|Тапани|ml|ഡ്രം|mn|Бөмбөр|mos|Lunga|mr|ड्रम|ms|Dram|my|စည်|nah|Huehuetl|nds|Trumm|new|द्रम|nl|Trommel|nn|Tromme|no|Tromme|oc|Tambor|os|Гуымсæг|pa|ਢੋਲ|pap|Tambòr|pl|Bęben (muzyka)|pms|Tamborn|pnb|ڈھول|pt|Tambor|qu|Wankar|ro|Tobă|ru|Барабан|rue|Бубны|sah|Барабаан|scn|Tammuru|sd|ڊرم|sh|Bubanj|simple|Drum|sk|Bubon (hudba)|sl|Boben|sn|Ngoma|so|Durbaan|sq|Daullja|sr|Бубањ|su|Drum|sv|Trumma|sw|Ngoma (ala)|ta|நூதன முரசு|tg|Барабан|th|กลอง|tl|Tambol|tok|poki kalama|tr|Davul|uk|Барабан|ur|ڈرم|uz|Baraban (cholgʻu asbobi)|vi|Trống|wa|Tabeur|war|Kombo|wuu|鼓|yi|פויק|zgh|ⴰⵏⴳⵏⴰⴳ|zh|鼓|zh_min_nan|Kó͘|zh_yue|鼓|zu|Isigubhu|qid=Q11404}}, {{ill|Shōko (instrument)|Q3482784|qid=Q3482784}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=sasara}}, and {{ill|Flute|Q11405|qid=Q11405}}{{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=184}}. Three large mikoshi and two children's mikoshi travel round-trip to {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ozu Wakamiya Shrine}} in Akanoi about 1 km away<ref name=":2" />.

Such dances are called {{ill|Furyū-odori|Q11665528|qid=Q11665528}} and are said to have spread from Kyoto across Shiga in the early modern period{{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=184}}.

=== Cultural properties ===
[[ファイル:Statue of Ukanomitama at Ozu-jinja.jpg|thumb|Wooden seated Ukanomitama statue (Important Cultural Property)]]
=== Important Cultural Property ===
* Wooden seated statue of Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto
: The goddess statue enshrined in the honden is estimated to date from the mid-{{ill|Heian period|Q193292|qid=Q193292}} and is designated {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|Q1188622|qid=Q1188622}}{{Sfn|滋賀県教育委員会事務局文化財保護課|2019|p=184}}. It is a painted wooden image about 50 cm high with a lotus crown, left hand holding a jewel on a raised left knee<ref name=":0" />. It is counted among three deity statues together with examples at {{ill|Matsunoo Taisha|Q710302|qid=Q710302}} and {{ill|Yakushi-ji|Q945913|qid=Q945913}}<ref name=":0" />.
